Guide 08 / 10

A one-sheet home electricity audit

Build a small record you can improve over time instead of guessing which device caused a bill.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Record checkable inputs

Start with device name, quantity, watts from a label or meter, active hours per day, days used, and where each number came from. Mark figures that are still guesses. You do not need to list every outlet on day one; start with devices used frequently or for long periods.

Separate estimate types

For steady loads, calculate watts × hours × days ÷ 1,000. For variable loads, prefer label kWh or a meter reading when available. For standby, record standby hours separately from active hours. Add device estimates only when their periods match.

Compare with the main meter

Your sum can differ from the main meter because you missed loads, label ratings differ from real draw, or dates do not match. The gap is a prompt to improve your record, not proof of a billing error. Keep dates so your comparison can be repeated.

A worked example

Example columns: device | units | W | hours/day | days | estimated kWh | source of figure | operating-mode note.

Avoid this mistake

Common error: adding kWh from different periods and comparing the sum with one monthly bill.
